clue.text: African country, say, surrounded by twisting roads

indicators.note: something twisting is bent out of its straight line, so these letters are set in a new order
whatever is surrounded sits within an outer ring, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: lanes are narrow roads
e.g. means 'for example', which is what 'say' means here

explanation.surface: A traveller describes some African nation hemmed in by winding roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' is the stock way of signalling an example, so it stands for the abbreviation for 'for example'. The rearranged roads are split around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a republic on the western coast of Africa, with Dakar as its capital.

clue.text: Unconscious mental pressure to have a drink before attempt

blocks.note: to sup is to drink, usually in small mouthfuls
ere is an old word for before
to have a go is to make an attempt

explanation.surface: Some inner urge pushes a person to have a drink before trying something difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' looks like a link word ordering the events, but it supplies the poetic word for earlier; the whole clue reads straight through in order.
explanation.definitionFit: In Freudian theory the superego is the part of the psyche that acts as a moral conscience, pressing on the mind largely below awareness.

clue.text: Tiny molecule never found in form of butane

indicators.note: a form of something is a new shape made from the same material, so the letters are rearranged
what is found in something lies inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written, a gas used as fuel
'never!' and 'no!' are both flat refusals

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: some small molecule is never present in any form of butane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form of butane' sounds like real chemistry, which hides the anagram. A refusal slips in after the second letter of the rearranged gas.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanotube is a cylindrical carbon structure only nanometres across, effectively one very small, very long molecule.

clue.text: Revolutionary in leaving place for boat tidy

indicators.note: a revolution turns things right round, so the result is read backwards
what is leaving goes away, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: a mooring is a spot where a boat is tied up
taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: A rebel slips away from the harbour berth, leaving the boat tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a noun for a rebel, but it signals turning the shortened berth word round. 'In' is not a link word here; it is the letters removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom is to make neat and smart, as when brushing hair or a horse's coat, so it works as a verb meaning tidy.

clue.text: Severe punishment having caught one neglecting entomology for biology?

indicators.note: to have caught something is to take it in, so new letters come into the phrase
what is neglected is left out, so some letters are dropped to make room

blocks.note: a life sentence is the heaviest prison term a court can give
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
the Roman numeral for one
the opening three letters of the word for the study of insects

explanation.surface: A harsh penalty for someone who skipped insect studies in favour of biology.
explanation.walkthrough: In LIFE SENTENCE the ENT is swapped for C and I. The question mark marks biology as just one example of the answer, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Life sciences are the branches of science dealing with living things, and biology is the central example of the group.

clue.text: US city cross with company importing silver

indicators.note: to import is to bring goods inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: chi is the Greek letter written as a cross, X
Co. is the abbreviation for company
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: An American city is annoyed with a firm that brings in silver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry, but it is the Greek letter shaped like an X. Ag for silver comes from the Latin argentum.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is the largest city in Illinois, on the shore of Lake Michigan.

clue.text: Tea, hot, served in Central America …

indicators.note: a thing served in a vessel sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
CA is the abbreviation for Central America

explanation.surface: A hot cup of tea is poured out somewhere in Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into the next clue, but this clue is complete by itself. Cha is the slangy British spelling also seen as char.
explanation.definitionFit: Cha is an informal British word for tea, borrowed from the Chinese name for the drink.

clue.text: … as a result of American engaging in various topics

indicators.note: various means mixed and assorted, so the letters are jumbled into a new order
to engage in something is to get inside it, so one piece enters the other

blocks.note: taken as written, part of the jumbled letters
A is the abbreviation for American
taken as written, the rest of the jumbled letters

explanation.surface: Following on from the tea clue, an American joins in a chat on all sorts of subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' looks like it belongs with 'as a result', but it joins TOPICS in the jumble, with A placed inside. The leading ellipsis just links the surface to the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipso facto is Latin for 'by that very fact', used in English to mean by direct consequence.

clue.text: Cheers when splitting a variable screen image

indicators.note: what splits something wedges into its middle, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: taken as written
var is the standard short form of variable
ta is British slang for thank you

explanation.surface: People cheer as some ever-changing picture appears on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' is not applause but the British way of saying thank you, which is also ta. It splits the abbreviated variable after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: An avatar is the picture or figure a user chooses to represent themselves on a computer or game display.

clue.text: Upset, not working? Stop working

blocks.note: a machine that is off is not working
to end is to finish or cease, as when stopping work

explanation.surface: An irritated worker, the machine broken, decides to down tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' could be an adjective, but the definition is the verb: to upset someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend someone is to hurt their feelings or annoy them, the transitive sense of the verb upset.

clue.text: Long to get over theatrical production

blocks.note: to pant for something is to long for it
O is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to get past a stage show they dread.
explanation.walkthrough: A panto (pantomime) is a British family Christmas stage show of fairy tales, slapstick and audience shouting. 'Over' as O comes from cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for pantomime, it is a staged comic show put on in British theatres each winter season.

clue.text: Display area marks Welsh river

blocks.note: to flag something is to mark it for attention
the Taff is the river that flows through Cardiff

explanation.surface: Scoring signs set up by a Welsh river for some show.
explanation.walkthrough: Like several answers here, this is a US city too (in Arizona), but the definition takes the pole sense: the place where a flag is shown off.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagstaff is the pole a flag flies from, so it is the spot where a banner is put on show.

clue.text: Again measures length of house, returning after getting retired

indicators.note: something returning heads back the way it came, so it is read backwards

blocks.note: ret. is the abbreviation for retired
a semi is a semi-detached house, one of a joined pair

explanation.surface: A pensioner, back home, measures the house once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Length of house' looks like a single idea, but the definition stops at 'length of'. A semi is the British name for a semi-detached house.
explanation.definitionFit: To retime an event is to clock its duration a second time, so the answer means timing it once more.

clue.text: Hold back official description of poor weather?

blocks.note: a ref is a referee, a match official
rain is a standard example of bad weather

explanation.surface: A clue posing as a riddle: what would an official forecast call bad weather?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a definition of one weather term, but it is two pieces: a match official and wet weather.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain is to stop yourself from doing something, holding back from an action or impulse.

clue.text: Unexpectedly it curtails retaining expression of individuality following religious practice

indicators.note: to retain is to keep hold of, so one piece is held inside the other
something unexpected comes out differently from how it started, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
saying 'I' expresses the self as an individual

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a rite unexpectedly cuts short any show of personality.
explanation.walkthrough: The added I joins the letters of IT CURTAILS before they are all reshuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritualistic describes behaviour that sticks closely to set ceremonies and rites, especially in worship.

clue.text: Get angry about the Earth with shifting of a lake - one’s joining movement

indicators.note: shifting a lake's letter means moving it to a new spot, so the order of letters changes

blocks.note: global means concerning the whole world
one's read as 'I is', I for one plus S
a tic is an involuntary twitching movement

explanation.surface: An environmental protester is furious about the planet and about a lake being moved.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one letter shifts: in the worldwide word, the L for lake moves along to sit after the A. 'Movement' is a twitch, not a campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: To go ballistic is an idiom for flying into a sudden rage, like a missile shooting off.

clue.text: American aboard drifting Italian ship sunk during war

indicators.note: something drifting wanders out of position, so the letters move into a new order
whoever is aboard is inside the vessel, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
US is short for American, as in the United States

explanation.surface: An American travels on an Italian vessel adrift, which was sunk in wartime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian ship' looks like part of the definition, but Italian is the anagram material. The rearranged letters take US after the first L.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lusitania was a British ocean liner torpedoed by a German submarine in 1915, during the First World War.

clue.text: Remote lake - it’s repeatedly brought up with two accounts raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up reads it from bottom to top, backwards
raised means lifted upward, which in a down entry reverses the letters

blocks.note: the word it, twice
ac is the abbreviation for account, taken twice

explanation.surface: A faraway lake keeps getting mentioned alongside a couple of financial accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pairs are reversed separately and then joined. The 's of it's is just 'is', a link in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Titicaca lies high in the Andes between Peru and Bolivia, far from most places, hence remote.

clue.text: Ancient city, source of history in times of horse-drawn transport?

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so only the opening letter is kept
one thing in another sits within it, so a piece is placed inside

blocks.note: a cart is a vehicle pulled by a horse
the first letter of history
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: An old city whose history goes back to the days of horse and cart.
explanation.walkthrough: CART AGE, the era of horse transport, takes H into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Carthage was the great Phoenician city of North Africa, destroyed by Rome in 146 BC.

clue.text: Reinterpreted a man’s action in Californian city

indicators.note: to reinterpret is to give a new reading, so the letters are read in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's behaviour is seen in a new light in a West Coast city.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored, so A MAN'S ACTION gives eleven letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Monica is a beach city on the Pacific coast, west of Los Angeles in California.

clue.text: Cool location initially has top entertainers

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letters are used

blocks.note: the first letters of both words
to own is to have

explanation.surface: A trendy venue boasts the best performers around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' does not mean best: it is the big top, the circus tent, where these performers work.
explanation.definitionFit: Clowns perform under the big top, the large circus tent, so they are literally entertainers of the top.

clue.text: Monster very active in West and North

indicators.note: active letters are lively and moving, so they shift into a new order
one thing in another sits within it, so a piece is placed inside

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for west
taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A beast is reported to be very busy across the west and north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very active' reads as one phrase, but 'active' works on the word before it. The result sits between W and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A wyvern is a heraldic and legendary winged dragon with two legs, a mythical monster.

clue.text: Still wearing recent baby clothes

indicators.note: a garment being worn wraps around its wearer, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: late can mean recent, as in 'the late news'
still and yet both mean up to now

explanation.surface: A child is still dressed in the latest baby outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' suggests clothes and fits the surface, but it is the containment signal. 'Recent' gives late in the sense of latest news.
explanation.definitionFit: A layette is a complete set of clothing and bedding prepared for a newborn child.

clue.text: Poet: one’s range covering start of sonnet

indicators.note: the start is the very beginning, so just the opening letter is kept
to cover something is to go over and around it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
an ambit is the scope or extent of something
the first letter of sonnet

explanation.surface: A poet's scope takes in the opening line of a sonnet.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of one's stands for 'has': one has AMBIT wrapped around S. The answer is a rare word worth learning.
explanation.definitionFit: An iambist is a writer of verse in iambs, the short-long metrical foot, so a kind of versifier.

clue.text: The writer’s intent on sending up US city

indicators.note: in a down entry, sending letters up means reading them from the bottom, so backwards

blocks.note: the writer is the setter, so 'the writer's' is I'm
your aim is your intent or purpose

explanation.surface: An author admits they mean to mock an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sending up' suggests mockery, but in a down clue it means turn upside down. 'The writer' standing for the setter, I, is a convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami is the large Florida city on the Atlantic coast, a major American urban centre.

clue.text: Minor recipient of honour this evening?

blocks.note: wee is Scottish for small
a knight has received a knighthood from the monarch

explanation.surface: A small-time knighthood is to be handed over tonight.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark says the definition is only an example: tonight may be any Monday to Friday night.
explanation.definitionFit: A weeknight is any evening from Monday to Friday, so tonight could well be one of them.

clue.text: Odd bits of energy recycled? That’s cool!

indicators.note: the odd bits are the first, third and fifth positions, so only those letters are kept
recycling sends material back round again, so the letters are read in the other direction

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters of energy

explanation.surface: An eco-enthusiast is thrilled by the idea of reusing bits of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking letters 1, 3 and 5 of ENERGY gives EEG, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Gee is a mild exclamation of surprise or admiration, the same kind of reaction as 'cool!'.

clue.text: Position taken for wellbeing as an Australian

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
A is the abbreviation for Australian; the letters running across the phrase are a coincidence of the charade, not a concealment

explanation.surface: An Australian adopts some posture for the sake of good health.
explanation.walkthrough: Almost all of the wordplay is taken as written, only Australian is shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: An asana is a posture held in yoga, practised for physical and mental health.

clue.text: Historic state capital certain to retain an opening for them

indicators.note: to retain is to keep hold of, so one piece is kept inside another
an opening is the way in, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: a safe bet is a certain one
taken as written
the first letter of them

explanation.surface: An old capital is sure to keep a way in for visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: A safe bet is a certain one; the inserted pair goes in after its first letter. The answer is two words, Spanish for holy faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Fe, founded in 1610, is the capital of New Mexico and the oldest state capital in the US.

clue.text: Political situation and other things swirling around South American capital

indicators.note: a swirl spins round on itself, so the letters come out in reverse order
around means encircling, so one piece goes on either side of another

blocks.note: etc. is short for et cetera, 'and other things'
Lima is the capital of Peru

explanation.surface: Political turmoil swirls around a Latin American capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' looks like a joining word, but 'and other things' is the full sense of ETC, with only 'other things' supplying it.
explanation.definitionFit: Climate in its figurative sense means the prevailing mood or conditions, as in the political climate.
